**Much faster, crash-safe, and a data fix.** Reading is about 18 times
faster, small files and folders several times faster, and a crash or power
cut can no longer scramble a drive. This release also fixes a bug, present
since v0.1.0, that padded shrunk files with zeros on Windows.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.1.2-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon + Intel) | `cloak-v0.1.2-macos-universal.zip` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

Each zip has `cloak` (CLI), `cloak-gui` (desktop app) and the mount adapter
(`cloak-winmount.exe` on Windows, `cloak-mount` on macOS). Keep them in the
same folder: the app launches the adapter from next to itself.

The binaries are not code-signed. On macOS, clear the download quarantine
before first run: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine cloak-v0.1.2-macos-universal`.

## Upgrade note

**Update every computer that shares a store to v0.1.2.** File sizes now come
from the disguised files themselves, and very large folders may have their
list split into parts. Older versions would show wrong sizes and can't read a
split list. Existing drives open as they are; nothing needs converting.

## Fixed

- **Shrunk files padded with zeros (Windows).** When an app made a file
  smaller, the drive kept it at the next multiple of 512 bytes, with zeros at
  the end. If you edit files in place on a v0.1.0 or v0.1.1 drive, check any
  that were saved smaller.

## Faster (measured on Windows, same disk)

| | v0.1.1 | v0.1.2 |
|---|---|---|
| Read a big file | 51 MB/s | 935 MB/s |
| Copy in 1,000 small files | 17–159 a second | 630 a second |
| Delete 1,000 files | 8.6–32 s | about 0.3 s |
| List a 5,000-file folder | 16 s | 13 ms |
| Random 4 KiB writes | — | 20,000 a second |

- Writes change only the bytes written and the encrypted ends, instead of
  rewriting the whole file when its size changes.
- Folder lists are kept in memory and saved half a second after they change,
  in one batch.
- Windows caches file data and details (but not folder listings, so file
  managers still update at once).
- Reads run in parallel on both Windows and macOS.

## Safer

- Folder lists and the store header are written so a crash leaves the old or
  the new version, never a torn one.
- Deletes and moves between folders are journaled and finished on the next
  mount if interrupted.
- A crash loses at most the last half-second of name changes, and never
  leaves a name pointing at nothing. Files an app has closed are always on
  the store.
- When a sync tool keeps two copies of a folder list (a sync conflict), they
  are merged on mount; a name clash becomes `name (conflict 1).ext`.
- Changes a sync tool brings in while the drive is mounted show up within a
  second.

## Known limitations

- **The macOS mount has still not been tested on a real Mac.** It builds and
  the shared engine is fully tested, but treat it as a preview and keep a
  backup of anything you put in a drive.
- A file created in the half-second before a crash may be lost, and its
  disguised file left behind unnamed in the store folder.
- FUSE-T is not supported yet (macFUSE only).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
